name: Selflessness
definition: You are humble when searching for the best ideas; you seek what's best for Netflix, not yourself or your team; you take time to help others succeed.

rows.situation: Choosing among ideas, including your own
rows.under: Pushes your idea because it is yours, and treats a better one as a loss.
rows.justRight: Drops your idea when another one is better for the company, and says whose idea it was.
rows.over: Refuses to advance any idea you thought of, so the team loses work you were actually the right person to do.

rows.situation: A choice that helps the company and slows your team
rows.under: Protects your team's numbers and leaves the company-level problem to someone else.
rows.justRight: Takes the company outcome when it is actually better, tells your team what you gave up, and helps them absorb it.
rows.over: Sacrifices your team's real commitments for a company story that does not change the outcome.

rows.situation: A colleague who is stuck on something you know
rows.under: Stays on your own list and lets them stay stuck.
rows.justRight: Takes the time to help them succeed, then goes back to your own work.
rows.over: Becomes the person everyone waits on, and your own work stops moving.

rows.situation: A win that started with someone else's idea
rows.under: Tells the story so the win sounds like yours.
rows.justRight: Names the person who had the idea and the people who made it real.
rows.over: Erases your own real contribution so thoroughly that nobody can see who did the work.

rows.situation: A meeting where you have part of the answer
rows.under: Stays quiet so you will look humble, and the worse idea wins.
rows.justRight: Offers what you know, then changes your mind in public if someone else has the better answer.
rows.over: Performs humility by agreeing with every speaker, and the decision never gets a real point of view.
